after: ## The six contexts as vocabulary organisers
alt: Six cards, one per global context, with example topics: friendship and online life; moving house and travel; music, festivals and hobbies; phones, social media and online learning; food waste, recycling and tourism; access to education, volunteering and fair trade.
caption: A context is a lens; topics are what you actually talk about.

after: ## The six contexts as vocabulary organisers
alt: Tourism sits at the centre with arrows to three contexts: orientation in space and time (journeys), globalization and sustainability (impact on places) and fairness and development (who benefits). One word bank can be angled towards each.
caption: Build a bank once and angle it towards different contexts.

alt: A word bank for food waste in six layers: core nouns (leftovers, packaging, compost), verbs in phrases (reduce waste, donate surplus food), describing words, opinion and linking phrases, chunks such as “make a difference”, and a scale row with one idea at personal, local and global level.
caption: Nouns alone will not carry you: add verbs, describers, linkers, chunks and scale.

alt: A small circle of productive vocabulary, the words you can use in speaking and writing, sits inside a larger circle of receptive vocabulary, the words you recognise in listening and reading. Listening and reading need breadth, including synonyms; speaking and writing need depth and accuracy.
caption: Your receptive bank is always bigger; practise producing to close the gap.

alt: One word bank feeds all four criteria: in listening, predict words and synonyms; in reading, use word families and context and watch for false friends; in speaking, recycle chunks and move from personal to local to global; in writing, use linking phrases, precise verbs and a steady register. The chunk “keep in touch with” is used across them.
caption: The same chunks reused in every skill move from recognised to usable.

alt: A timeline from day 1 to day 15: learn a set on day 1, then review on days 2, 4, 8 and 15. Each review tests from English first and keeps missed words in a “tricky” column; before an assessed task, rebuild the topic bank from memory for five minutes.
caption: Learn on day 1, then review on days 2, 4, 8 and 15.
